outcome_neutrality: Both fix diffs verified by full read: neither touches engines/, the four frozen contracts, sources/, data, costs, signal, folds, universe, direction or thresholds. git diff --name-only 1a3ec56c..f82121a7 => score_runner.py only. Engines byte-identical from 51547179 (r2-audited) through 84eaf6b1; contracts byte-identical since freeze commit 9f14a73a.

The CAGR guard changes only the representation of an undefined CAGR (crash -> null + note); gross/costs/net/PF/win-rate/folds/verdict are computed before and untouched by it; the per-cell verdict derives from the net sign alone, so the guard cannot alter any verdict. For FXNG3 (net=+0.1067>0) the guard is inert and returns the same number attempt 1 computed.

This is NOT the forbidden 'rerun for bad results': the rerun recovered persistence of a crashed atomic job with unchanged frozen inputs and deterministic code; the bad outcome (CNG2 NET_NEGATIVE) was nonetheless re-computed, persisted and reported. No result-shopping channel exists: nothing was altered that could improve a number.

DISCLOSED PARTIAL LEAK ADJUDICATED: attempt 1's crash inference (CNG2 net < -1.0 from the complex domain, before persistence, disclosed in the 6320fa2d message) could not be acted on — every input it might influence (construction, costs, folds, universe, direction, thresholds) was frozen in commits that predate ANY outcome and verified byte-unchanged; the only decisions the leak could touch were whether to re-run (done, for persistence) or to suppress CNG2 (not done — NET_NEGATIVE reported honestly).
